author: manoelacs
body:
This pull request introduces significant changes to the project structure, styling, and functionality, focusing on modularizing components, implementing a theme context for dark mode, and updating CSS styles. Below are the most important changes:

### Component Modularization:

* [`src/App.tsx`](diffhunk://#diff-26ad4b834941d9b19ebf9db8082bd202aaf72ea0ddea85f5a8a0cb3c729cc6f2L3-R12): Replaced individual component imports (`Home`, `About`, `Projects`, `Contact`, `Footer`) with new modular components (`Header`, `Footer`, `PageLayout`).
* [`src/molecules/header.tsx`](diffhunk://#diff-a765161c8bf787674b0759bb7e2e2142ebd2196a6727047247e687dc57a19303R1-R23): Created a new `Header` component with a theme toggle button.
* [`src/molecules/pageLayout.tsx`](diffhunk://#diff-aeb8057c36891b67fc9222a5cabb437f48eafcec2cc525c985746bf6fb343d6dR1-R16): Added a new `PageLayout` component to structure the page layout with `Navbar`, `PageSection`, and `SideMenu`.

### Theme Context Implementation:

* [`src/themeContext.tsx`](diffhunk://#diff-811b384d2f71e0c4c0cb9f163edd488af085fe0ef3372a75d6d3f573568a2d10R1-R42): Introduced a `ThemeContext` to manage theme state and provide a toggle function.
* [`src/atoms/themeButton.tsx`](diffhunk://#diff-46fedf418ca86ec46f8ff0fede0b8b79e7566c858bbf3fe3ecb8e3ca1685d97cR1-R18): Added a `ThemeButton` component that uses `ThemeContext` to switch between light and dark themes.
* [`src/main.tsx`](diffhunk://#diff-1cd8b18798a1a103bfe13bef54354c1f3a3bea29a31c8eea1a0c67a3a839b811R5-R11): Wrapped the `App` component with `ThemeProvider` to provide theme context throughout the application.

### CSS and Styling Updates:

* [`src/App.css`](diffhunk://#diff-60f5dcfc15327d5dd812d9df394c217efbedb4aa33dca782ed69d39dce811972L2-L41): Updated the root styling to support dark mode and removed unused styles.
* [`src/index.css`](diffhunk://#diff-85da366246340e911d7a0eb9153e64137a1b31f0686c74d9aef9ae4f032cb09eR2): Imported additional Google Fonts for enhanced typography.

### Component Removal:

* Removed old components (`Home`, `About`, `Projects`, `Contact`, `Footer`, `Header`) from the `src/components` directory as they were replaced by the new modular components. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-febe472312c34362d6340a54dd876572b5ef8731d37a0d895c9b6b1f2ead8a8eL1-L11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8387d64f5b5e50e1e386a42e75a377d0d8bf6d40a149697aca42cfeda4c8c206L1-L36) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-bbfcb62cfc4b5e3cb8e7347614b1d8f05d1f77efa9272b31b4f03ce532929f8cL1-L21)

### Alias Update:

* [`vite.config.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-6a3b01ba97829c9566ef2d8dc466ffcffb4bdac08706d3d6319e42e0aa6890ddL14-R14): Updated the alias configuration to use `@src` instead of `@` for better clarity and consistency.

author: kicanter
body:
Refs: Issues #30 and #19

This pull request is a small but powerful update. There are two large feature enhancements along with README updates.

* react-swipeable has been replaced with Embla Carousel for swipe gestures. The only gestures that are implemented have to do with page navigation, and Embla Carousel is a lightweight and contained tool that helped me to easily integrate a smooth and consistent tab bar carousel into the mobile navigation.
* To accommodate iOS users, the mobile gyroscope/orientation tilt effect has been forfeited in favor of a draggable card tilt feature. To prevent interference with the carousel swiping or refresh gesture, the user must swipe up to activate the card's rotation, and successive dragging will control the rotation of the card up to a ceiling of 15°.

author: mdhaber
body:
numpy/numpy#27771 allows `default_rng` to accept instances of `RandomState` and convert them to a `Generator`. This updates the SPEC accordingly.

*Update: before merge, also correct single-backtick `Generator` in suggested `rng` documentation:*

> Types other than `numpy.random.Generator` are passed to `numpy.random.default_rng` to instantiate a `Generator`.

*This looks fine in markdown, but in ReST it needs two backticks.*

---

The first stage of SciPy's SPEC 7 transition is essentially complete:
https://github.com/scipy/scipy/issues/21833

For standard cases, other libraries might be interested in how we extended the decorator to inject standard documentation about the transition, e.g.

![{EB7EB439-218F-4660-8B30-EF4BDE09EB49}](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d83245a-8cb2-46b8-9caf-9968b8f42ec6)

We also added standard tests:
https://github.com/scipy/scipy/blob/82ee02556872b9f91576b835a8f40f1d9eb1fd8d/scipy/_lib/tests/test__util.py#L556

It also might be useful to see in how we handled some of the oddball cases, like `seed` arguments that already converted integers to `Generators` (instead of `RandomState`), existing `rng` arguments that worked more like most legacy `seed`/`random_state` arguments, and `random_state` attributes of classes, but I'm not sure if all that can be summarized.

author: robertocastro391
body:
# Pull Request Summary

## Overview

This pull request introduces a new endpoint for uploading contracts, along with the necessary error handling and database updates.

### 1. Created Endpoint for Contract Upload
The following endpoint has been added:

#### houses/uploadContract
- **Method**: POST
- **Description**: This endpoint allows the upload of a contract file and associated contract data. The contract is stored in an S3 bucket, and the file URL is saved in the database for the corresponding tenant. The endpoint accepts contract data as a JSON string (`contract_data`) and the contract file (`file`) as input.

#### Key Functionality:
- **Contract Data Parsing**: The contract data is passed as a JSON string, which is parsed into a `ContractCreate` model.
- **File Upload**: The contract file is uploaded to an S3 bucket. The filename is formatted to replace spaces with underscores (`_`).
- **Tenant Association**: The contract URL is associated with the tenant's record in the database. If the tenant does not exist, a 404 error is raised.

### 2. Created Endpoint Tests
#### Files Created/Updated:
- **tests/routes/test_contract_routes.py**

#### Purpose:
- Added tests for the `/uploadContract` endpoint to ensure that contract data and file uploads are handled correctly.

#### Implementation:
- **Tested Contract Upload**: Verified that the endpoint successfully handles contract file uploads and associates them with the correct tenant.
- **Error Handling**: Added tests for invalid JSON input, missing tenants, and S3 upload failures.

### 3. Database Setup Improvements
- Updated the `Tenents` table to include a reference to the contract URL.
- Enhanced the schema to store contract-related data for tenants.

author: darrenedale
body:
`IsTypedArray` validation rule requires an array whose items are all of a given type. The type can be a scalar built-in, a class built-in or a user-defined class.

`partition()` helper function takes any iterable and classifies them according to a classification function. It returns the items from the iterable partitioned into _n_ arrays, where _n_ is the number of unique return values from the classification function given each of the items in the array. Each item ends up in just one of the returned arrays, according to the return value of the classification function for that item.

author: awallace77
body:
Closes #14 
Closes #33 
Closes #39 

# Overview
_The below points refer to the `HealthMetricCalculator` class._
- Created `calculateOrganHealth` function that accepts a single scan and populates the output parameter with `HealthMetricModel` objects of the health of each organ. The calculation was done using a 20% rule where any measurement that differs by more than 20% of the mean is considered an outlier. Populates an output parameter with `HealthMetricModel` objects indicating the organ name, value, description indicating organ level, and an integer value of +1, -1, or 0 to indicate above, below, or normal levels.
- Created `calculateIndicatorHealth` function that accepts a single scan, calculating the indicator health (energy level, metabolism, immune system, musculoskeletal, and psycho-emotional) and populating an output parameter with `HealthMetricModel` objects. Each indicator has a 'normal level' range. After calculating each indicator, we check if the values are in the range. Similar to the `calculateOrganHealth`, we populate an output parameter with `HealthMetricModel` objects indicating the indicator name, indicator value, description (normal, above normal, below normal), and an integer value corresponding to their level of abnormality  (+1, -1, or 0 to indicate above, below, or normal).
- Created `calculateTrendHealth` function that accepts a vector of Scans and an output parameter to hold the health metrics. **Please note** the vector of Scans is assumed to be in order from oldest to newest scan (index 0 holds the oldest scan). The function simply generates a list for each indicator health metric from the scans. Using this data, we find the slope for each indicator to determine if the measurements are trending up, down, or staying level. The output parameter is then populated with `HealthMetricModel` objects indicating the trend name, the indicator's most recent value (from the most recent scan), a description of the trend, and an integer representation of the trend (+1 for up, -1 for down, and 0 for level).


# Other Updates
- major updates to the ScanModel and Scan table schema

body:
# Implementation of Core Smart Contracts for Luxury Fashion Authentication Platform

## Overview
This PR implements four foundational smart contracts for our luxury fashion authentication platform on the Stacks blockchain. Each contract serves a specific purpose in creating a secure, modular system for luxury fashion authentication.

## Core Contracts Implemented

### 1. SIP009 NFT Trait Contract (`sip009-nft-trait.clar`)
- Defines the standard NFT interface
- Implements required SIP009 functions:
  - get-last-token-id
  - get-token-uri
  - get-owner
  - transfer
- Ensures compatibility with Stacks NFT ecosystem

### 2. Fashion Item Contract (`fashion-item.clar`)
- Manages core fashion item data structures
- Implements item tracking functionality
- Handles:
  - Item registration
  - Item metadata storage
  - Ownership records
  - Item ID management

### 3. Authentication Contract (`authentication.clar`)
- Manages verification records
- Handles authorized verifier registry
- Implements:
  - Verifier authorization system
  - Authentication record keeping
  - Verification status tracking

### 4. Luxury Authentication Contract (`luxury-auth.clar`)
- Main business logic contract
- Integrates functionality from other contracts
- Implements:
  - Item registration workflow
  - Transfer mechanisms
  - Verification processes
  - Administrative controls

## Technical Implementation Details

### Contract Architecture
```
contracts/
├── sip009-nft-trait.clar    # NFT standard interface
├── fashion-item.clar        # Item data management
├── authentication.clar      # Verification system
└── luxury-auth.clar         # Main business logic
```

### Key Functions by Contract

**Fashion Item Contract:**
- Item registration
- Metadata management
- Ownership tracking

**Authentication Contract:**
- Verifier management
- Authentication records
- Verification status

**Luxury Auth Contract:**
- Business logic integration
- Transfer mechanics
- Administrative controls

**SIP009 NFT Trait:**
- Standard NFT interface
- Token management interface

## Security Considerations
- Modular design for isolated security boundaries
- Contract-specific access controls
- Cross-contract call security
- Principal-based authentication

## Testing
Contracts have been tested both individually and for integration:
- Unit tests for each contract
- Integration tests for cross-contract calls
- Access control verification
- Error handling scenarios

## Next Steps
- Marketplace contract implementation
- Frontend integration
- Enhanced cross-contract functionality
- Additional authentication features

## Dependencies
- Clarinet
- Stacks 2.4
- SIP009 NFT standard

<details>
<summary>stakater/Reloader (reloader)</summary>

### [`v1.2.0`](https://redirect.github.com/stakater/Reloader/releases/tag/v1.2.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/stakater/Reloader/compare/v1.1.0...v1.2.0)

#### Announcement :loudspeaker: :loudspeaker: :loudspeaker:

From this release onwards, helm charts and images/git releases will have different semver versioning. If you are using git releases as a reference for helm charts, it will break in the future.
It is recommended to make changes to your workflows to accommodate these changes for smooth upgrades in the future.

Changes were made to the understanding of our mistakes in treating both helm chart and git releases as related artifacts so they had the same versioning on releases, which we consider is wrong and we are attempting to fix it.

Apologies in advance for trouble, if any.

author: incodame
body:
New syntax for pavements for use in the paragraph tool:
 - dcg capture variables - similar principle to the regex() loc using V1L
 - isa property for parameter: reference to a definition in the pavement referred by the prefix (e.g. "java:" )
 - a structure can use a loc of type q() to refer to the variables defined by the reference (prolog query)
 - sub-parameters can use a loc of type q() (to form a conjunction with the parent structure query)
 - list of sub-params can use the syntax: - <renamed param>: param(<param>) to provide a context and avoid duplicate definitions (e.g.  in maven.yml: parent_group_id and dep_group_id refer to a single group_id sub param definition)

Added consistency check of cross-references in a pavement definition
